course_name: Connected study workflow - original neutral demonstration

bilingual.title: Build a connected study route
terms: Consecutive source ideas answering one shared question.
The connection from a previous conclusion to the next question.
A task that uses the ideas just explained.

notes.label: Prerequisite bridge
notes.text: Read the whole source before teaching its parts. A formula, argument, code trace or procedure belongs in the knowledge block it helps explain. Keep the source order and make each transition explicit.

homework.label: Practice connection
homework.text: The complete original practice question is on study-guide page 6. Its final part asks you to distinguish a source-check record from evidence about reasoning and to choose one useful next action.
homework.source: Original neutral fixture; full question page 6, solution pages 6-7.

bilingual.title: Check what the source log covers
terms: The top number: checked items C.
The bottom number: all listed items N, which must be positive.
A fraction expressed as an amount per hundred.

notes.label: What the symbols and counts mean
notes.text: N is the distinct listed count; C is the checked count; q is the checked fraction. The pictured log is synthetic. Its 6 of 8 checked items give 75% source-check coverage, not a score for understanding or learning quality.

homework.label: Practice connection
homework.text: Part (a) resets the example to N = 10 and C = 7. Use the same definition, substitute the new values, then convert the resulting share to a percentage. Do not carry over 6 and 8.
homework.source: Definition page 3; complete question and guided solution pages 6-7.

bilingual.title: Use the record to choose a next step
terms: A listed item still awaiting its source check; count U.
What remains of a whole after one part is removed.
A label identifying a particular value, such as log A or B.

notes.label: Connect the relation to its conditions
notes.text: The new symbol r is the pending fraction, U divided by N. The two groups cover the same nonempty list without overlap, so q + r = 1. Page 4 derives the connection one step at a time. A checked item can still need explanation or practice.

homework.label: Practice connection
homework.text: Parts (b)-(c) find the pending count and fraction, then check that both shares total one. Part (d) interprets the result. Page 8 compares two fresh logs and shows why larger counts and larger fractions answer different questions.
homework.source: All public slides, illustrations and questions are independently authored neutral fixtures.
